question: The class played the model's game with the opening line of Zora Neale Hurston's novel: "Ships at a distance have every man's wish on ____." Which three kinds of knowledge did the lecture say you needed just to play?

options.text: Spelling, punctuation, and a large vocabulary
options.feedback: None of these were the point. You could have guessed a noun with a modest vocabulary; what mattered was knowing what kind of word fits, what the sentence is about, and how a writer like Hurston would finish it.

options.text: Syntax, semantics, and style with world knowledge
options.feedback: You knew the slot needed a noun (syntax), that the noun should concern ships and wishing (semantics), and that 'board' is the poetic choice a novelist would make (style and world knowledge). A model has to learn all three to guess well.

options.text: The author's biography, the novel's title, and its publication year
options.feedback: Knowing about Hurston helps with the last step, but the game was not trivia. Nobody needed the title or the year to know that a noun about ships belonged there.

options.text: Syntax, semantics, and a memory of having read the novel
options.feedback: The first two are right, and the third is the tempting swap. You did not need to have read Hurston to play; you needed a sense of how writers choose words and of the world the sentence describes, which is the third thing the model has to learn.
